mechanism: Multiplicity-averaged sampled gradients and ordinary particle Adam. Before its update, compute active-row latent Gaussian-kernel densities using bandwidth median(pairwise squared distances)/log(active_rows+1), bounded below by optimizer epsilon. Postcondition each row displacement with inverse sqrt density, normalized to RMS multiplier one over active rows. No clipping and no direct repulsive force; all movement remains derived from GAN/unchanged auxiliary gradients.
rationale: Moment clocks and shared-coordinate/covariance changes all preserve unequal mass but cannot recover ring coverage. Test spatially differentiated mobility: isolated latent particles should not receive the same movement suppression as crowded ones. Particle positions and gradients only; no targets, mode labels, centers, real statistics or metrics.
optimizer_updates: One D plus one G/particle update per frozen iteration; particle custom update substitutes original Adam table update.
extra_work: O(A^2*d) pairwise latent distances, O(A^2) kernel/median/reduction, plus table clone and row displacement scaling; A is active rows, never an added sampled batch. No network forwards/backwards or optimizer steps added. Equal-step, not equal-compute. Own-state serialization is observation-only.
